 First Alert Weather: Why Middle Tennessee won’t see freeze warnings until April 
 Freezing temperatures are inevitable as we head towards winter, but don’t expect frost or freeze warnings from the National Weather Service until next spring. 
 By Bree Smith Published : Oct. 28, 2026 at 5:24 PM CDT | Updated : 30 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WSMV) - Freezing temperatures are inevitable as we conclude Fall and head into winter, but don’t expect any frost or freeze warnings until April, according to the National Weather Service in Nashville this fall or winter.
 Most weather warnings are for the impacts the weather may have on people, but frost and freeze warnings are issued to protect agriculture and sensitive plants during the growing season.
 For Middle Tennessee, the growing season concludes in early October, so the National Weather Service in Nashville ends its frost and freeze alert program on October 1.
 Since temperatures didn’t get cold enough to warrant a frost advisory or freeze warning before October 1 this year, those alerts won’t be issued again until the growing season resumes next April.
